pr.title: Post and lift a pull request's hold with one Projector command
pr.head: 3badd7c898d40410a347a23ce596489bd1142e24

summary: Projector's review loop marks a pull request ready when a review of its current head finds nothing open. The fix loop, fix-pr, sometimes builds a change that no review has read yet, such as a suggestion it decided to implement. While it does, it holds the pull request: it posts an issue comment by the pull request's author whose last line is <!-- projector-hold v=1 -->, and keeps the pull request a draft. project review publish, project review status, and the review watcher all read that comment and keep a held pull request in draft however clean its review is.

Until now fix-pr posted, edited, and deleted that comment with raw gh api calls. Claude Code's auto mode refused the deletion as a write to an external system, so a clean pull request stayed stuck in draft. This pull request moves the hold into one CLI command, project review hold, and adds one narrow permission rule for it, as Projector already does for the two publish commands.

• --add TEXT posts the hold, or adds changes to the open one, reads the comment back, and only then marks the pull request draft.
  • --drop TEXT removes changes the owner will not build from every hold comment that lists them, and deletes a comment left with none. The hold ends only once no hold comment is left.
  • A bare --drop ends the hold: it deletes every hold comment by the author. The command does not check that the push carrying the changes has happened; fix-pr runs it only after that push.

Every mode refuses unless the signed-in gh account is the pull request's author, and no mode marks a pull request ready. The command acts on the repository --repo names, or else on the origin of the checkout it runs in; unlike review status, it never takes a repository from review state on this machine. The readers of the hold are unchanged.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Hold: an issue comment by the pull request's author ending in the hold marker. While one is open, a clean review leaves the pull request a draft.
  • Operator: the account whose pull requests the loops work on, and the one gh is signed in as.
  • Allow rule: an entry in the user's Claude Code settings or Codex rules that lets a command run without the host's automatic approval check.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• 0a3b69b: one finding. Without --repo, hold took the repository from any review of the same pull request number set up on this machine before the checkout's origin, so it could hold or lift a pull request in another repository.
  • 126bf8e: the finding is fixed. hold now acts only on --repo or the checkout's origin. Clean, with four suggestions in the review body.
  • 6ce8bcb: the author held the pull request and carried out all four suggestions. Clean. The pull request stays a draft until the author lifts the hold.
  • 3badd7c: at the owner's request, --lift became a bare --drop, and the head check and the recorded head were removed. Clean.

groups.title: The hold command
groups.kicker: project review hold: post, extend, shrink, or end a hold
intro: The command lives in review.py beside holds(), the function every reader already uses to find a hold. cli.py adds the subcommand, with --add and --drop as a required, mutually exclusive pair; --drop takes an optional value, and a bare --drop ends the hold, and shares the pr, --repo, --state-dir, and --json arguments with review status.

The order inside --add is the point of the design. To the review watcher, a pull request that turns draft on an unchanged head with no hold open looks like an author who answered without pushing, so it asks for a re-review. The comment must therefore land, and read back with the marker on its last line, before the pull request is drafted.

checks.text: A hold is still found by the marker alone, through holds(), which keeps only the author's comments. The command parses the bullets of a comment it edits, so a hold posted by hand before this change can be extended or dropped from as well.

files.note: The command: hold checks the author and dispatches to hold_add, hold_drop, and hold_end; write_hold and read_hold write and verify the comment.

checks.text: Every mode compares the signed-in login with the pull request's author before it reads or writes a comment. test_refuses_anyone_but_the_author runs all three modes as a non-author and checks that nothing is written, edited, deleted, or drafted.

The draft call comes only after the comment is written, read back with the marker last, and found to record the current head. test_posts_the_hold_then_drafts_the_pull_request checks the call order, and test_a_hold_that_does_not_read_back_drafts_nothing checks that a mangled comment drafts nothing.

A bare --drop ends the hold through hold_end, which deletes every hold comment by the author with no check of the head. The owner chose to trust the caller: fix-pr step 5 and docs/cli.md say to run it only after the push that carries every listed change, because a hold ended on the unchanged head lets a clean review of that head mark the pull request ready while the changes are still local.

hold_repo takes --repo, else the checkout's origin, and never reads review state. With review state for another repository's pull request of the same number present, the review confirmed that find_repo still returns that repository for status while hold_repo returns the checkout's own. test_a_review_set_up_for_the_same_number_in_another_repository_is_ignored covers it.

--drop now works across every hold comment by the author: it refuses a change none lists, rewrites each comment that lists a dropped change, deletes one left empty, and reports ended only when no hold comment is left. test_drop_works_across_every_hold_comment_and_ends_the_hold_only_when_none_is_left covers an older hand-written hold beside a newer one.

files.note: Adds the hold subcommand, which takes no --state-dir and is dispatched before the state directory is read, and reuses permissions.COMMANDS in two help strings. The rules docstrings now call the set Projector's permission rules.

checks.text: The first review flagged that hold resolved its repository through find_repo, which reads review state. This line now calls hold_repo, which does not.

A bare --drop appends None, which differs from the default [], so argparse counts it as given: it satisfies the required group, and --add x --drop exits 2. The review ran both, and --drop beside --drop TEXT in either order is refused before any GitHub call.

groups.title: The allow rule
groups.kicker: One more rule in the user's Claude Code settings and Codex rules
intro: project init, run by a person at a terminal, adds allow rules to the user's own settings so the host's automatic approval does not refuse a Projector command the user asked for. This change adds Bash(project review hold *) to the Claude Code rules and a second prefix_rule for ["project", "review", "hold"] to Projector's Codex rules file. project review rules now reports a settings file that lacks the new rule, so a user with only the two publish rules is asked to run init again.

files.note: Adds the hold rule to RULES, CODEX_PREFIX_RULES, the Codex rules file, and COMMANDS, and updates the messages that name them.

checks.text: The Codex rule allows only project review hold. test_codex_allows_exactly_the_publish_and_hold_commands_under_the_rules ran codex execpolicy check during the review and found no allowance for project summary hold or project review release.

files.note: Init and rules tests for the third rule, including the Codex policy check.

groups.title: Skills and documentation
groups.kicker: fix-pr uses the command; the other skills and docs say so
intro: fix-pr's section "Hold the pull request while changes are built" now runs project review hold for every step, passing --repo each time, and tells a session not to fall back to a raw gh api call when the host refuses the command. review-pr, start-review-loop, start-fix-loop, and docs/plugins.md now say the hold is ended through the command. docs/cli.md documents the command, its output, its --json fields, and the new rule.

files.note: The hold procedure rewritten around --add, --drop TEXT, and a bare --drop that ends the hold after the push.

checks.text: fix-pr still passes --repo every time, now so the command works from any directory. Without it, the command acts on the checkout's origin.

files.note: Says the author ends the hold with the command.
The rules check now names the hold command, and the hold paragraph names the command and is rewrapped to the file's width.
